source: AI Video Bootcamp - 100 Elevenlabs Soundeffects Example Prompts
note: The course's 100 example prompts, verbatim, plus the pattern they all share. ElevenLabs' sound-effects model makes EFFECTS: it does not write music and it does not speak lines, and asking for either is the usual reason a generation comes back unusable.

pattern.shape: <source> <action, as an -ing verb> <space or acoustic treatment>
pattern.why: Measured across all 100: 81 carry an -ing action verb (a further one has only "being", a copula, which does not count), 92 carry a preposition, and all 100 carry at least one of an action, a placement or a qualifier. They run 4 to 9 words. So the hard rule is that it must describe an EVENT rather than an object; naming the space is advice, not a rule.

ancient.label: Ancient world
ancient.note: Stone, fire and crowds. Reverb is doing most of the work.

medieval.label: Medieval
medieval.note: Metal, weather and animals. Good source of impact accents.

war.label: Modern war
war.note: Distance and muffling. Note how often the effect is described as heard through something.

colonial.label: Colonial
colonial.note: Small, close, mechanical sounds - the useful half for quiet scenes.

transition.label: Transitions
transition.note: Not objects but MOMENTS: something stops, reverses or resets. These are cut sounds.

villain.label: Villain and menace
villain.note: Low frequencies and slow movement. Use sparingly or it reads as parody.

comedy.label: Comedy
comedy.note: The set that carries an animal video. Exaggeration is the point - 'with comedic echo', 'with absurd intensity'.

action.label: Action and drama
action.note: Impacts and swells. Almost all of these are accents, not beds.

magic.label: Magic and time
magic.note: Layered hums and pulses. The most abstract group - lean on the qualifier.

ambience.label: Ambience
ambience.role: The bed under the whole scene. Continuous, quiet, no events.
ambience.note: Generate long and loop it. If you notice it, it is too loud.

key.label: Key effect
key.role: The thing the scene is actually about - the action you can see.
key.note: Should land on the frame where the action happens, not near it.

accent.label: Accent
accent.role: The punctuation: the cut, the reveal, the punchline.
accent.note: One per scene at most. Two accents cancel each other out.
